Sound Club Samui is a large electronic-music club on Soi Green Mango in Chaweng, about 60 m up the lane from the Green Mango Club, and it is operating in late 2026: its next listed night is ESSENCE on Wednesday 4 November 2026, from 21:00 to 03:00. Listings give its hours as 22:00 until late every night, and it fills after about 02:00, when the Green Mango crowd moves on. On event nights women usually get in free and men pay 300–500 THB, including one drink.

Some older directories list "Sound Club" on Soi Green Mango as permanently closed. That refers to an earlier club of the same name; the current Sound Club Samui has posted guest-DJ nights throughout 2026 and is listed as open in guides updated in October 2026.

What it's like

Sound Club is the late, louder half of Soi Green Mango. It is a big room built around its sound system and lighting, with an LED wall and a dance floor that holds a large crowd; reviewers single out the sound, and several suggest ear plugs. Where the Green Mango Club plays mainstream party music, Sound Club's event nights book techno, house and underground electronic DJs, Thai and international, with sponsored nights from drinks brands. Regular nights lean more towards club hits and remixes.

It starts late even by Chaweng standards. Doors open at around 22:00, but the room is thin until about 01:00 and properly busy after 02:00, when people come on from the Green Mango Club and the beach bars. It is rated about 4.5 out of 5 from roughly 980 Google reviews, with praise for the DJs and the sound, while complaints include inconsistent door checks and the price of water and soft drinks.

Bring cash: foreign-card ATMs charge about 250 THB per withdrawal. Shops stop selling alcohol at midnight, but licensed clubs keep their own hours.

Tips and safety

  • Timing: if you only want one club, go after 01:00. Arriving at 22:00 means two hours in a near-empty room.
  • ID: door checks are inconsistent, which is a reason to carry ID, not to leave it. A laminated copy of your passport photo page works better than a photo on your phone.
  • Water: it is a hot, packed room late at night. Budget for water at club prices and drink it.
  • Your drink: the UK Foreign Office warns that drink spiking and drug-assisted sexual assault happen in Thai tourist areas, to men and women, most often near bars late at night. Watch your drink being poured and never leave it.
  • Drugs: Thailand's drug penalties are severe, police carry out urine tests at party venues, and vapes are illegal for tourists too. Read drugs and alcohol law on Samui before you go.
  • Touts and bills: ignore "VIP entry" offers on the soi; pay at the door. Pay per round and check your bill. More on Koh Samui scams.
  • Help: Tourist Police 1155, police 191, ambulance 1669.

Who it suits, and who should go elsewhere

Good for: techno and house fans; people who want to keep going after the Green Mango Club; groups staying in central Chaweng who can walk home.

Go elsewhere if: you want chart music and a free door every night (the Green Mango Club, 60 m down the lane); you want to be in bed by 01:00; you are under 20; or you want a beach or pool party (see Koh Samui beach clubs). For bigger electronic parties, the Koh Phangan jungle parties and the Half Moon Festival are a boat ride away; see Koh Samui parties.

Getting there and home

  • Walk: from Chaweng Beach Road, turn into Soi Green Mango and walk towards the sea; the club is part-way down the lane, before the Green Mango Club.
  • Grab: about 80–120 THB within Chaweng and 200–400 THB to Lamai or Bophut late at night. After 03:00 there are fewer drivers, so expect to wait.
  • Taxis: wait on Chaweng Beach Road. Samui taxis were told to use meters in a May 2026 crackdown, but most still quote fixed fares; agree the price first.
  • Songthaews: mostly stop by 20:00–22:00.
  • Scooters: don't ride home at dawn. Police checkpoints are common in Chaweng and on the ring road, the legal limit is 50 mg per 100 ml of blood (20 mg for under-20s and anyone without a valid licence, including visitors without a motorcycle licence), and insurance won't cover a drink-riding crash.
